$comment: Manual screen-reader passes over the same journey, recorded by the person who ran
them. Nothing generates this file and nothing can: a driver reports what the DOM
says, and what a screen reader actually announces is a different question that only
a person with one running can answer.
It is deliberately separate from journeys.json so that an automated run can never
look like assistive-technology coverage. An empty checks list publishes 'none
recorded', which is the honest state until somebody runs one and writes it down.
Add an entry with: reader, browser, platform, checkedAt (ISO date), the journey step
ids it covered, an outcome of passed | passed-with-notes | failed, and notes.
